subtype_term.preferred_term: spastic paraplegia, optic atropy, and neuropathy

term.label: spastic paraplegia, optic atropy, and neuropathy

value.description: SPOAN syndrome, caused by a homozygous 216-bp deletion in the non-coding region upstream of KLC2 that leads to KLC2 overexpression - a recessive disease mechanism acting through increased rather than lost gene product. KLC2 is a kinesin light chain, which is why it is bound on the kinesin-dependent axonal cargo transport node. ClinGen has no KLC2 gene-disease validity record. Note that the bound MONDO label carries the misspelling 'optic atropy'; it is copied here as the ontology's canonical label.

selected_evidence.snippet: SPOAN syndrome is a neurodegenerative disorder mainly characterized by spastic paraplegia, optic atrophy and neuropathy (SPOAN).

value.name: SPG74
value.description: SPG74, caused by a homozygous IBA57 donor splice-site mutation in a highly consanguineous family whose ten affected members had a childhood-onset SPOAN-like phenotype - spastic paraplegia with optic atrophy and peripheral neuropathy - progressing slowly into late adulthood. IBA57 is a mitochondrial iron-sulfur protein assembly factor, which is why it is bound on the mitochondrial iron-sulfur cluster assembly node. ClinGen curates IBA57 against mitochondrial disease (Definitive) rather than against an HSP entity.

assertion.name: IBA57
assertion.notes: The committed ClinGen snapshot curates IBA57 against mitochondrial disease (MONDO:0044970, Definitive, autosomal recessive) rather than against an HSP entity.

selected_evidence.snippet: We mapped this disorder to a locus on chromosome 1q and identified a homozygous donor splice-site mutation in the IBA57 gene

value.name: SPG54
value.description: SPG54, caused by recessive DDHD2 variants in four families. The defining report gives the core phenotype as very early-onset spastic paraplegia with intellectual disability and a specific pattern of brain abnormalities on imaging, and reports an abnormal lipid peak on cerebral magnetic resonance spectroscopy as a distinguishing biomarker. DDHD2 encodes an intracellular phospholipase A1, which is why it is bound on the membrane-lipid node. ClinGen has no DDHD2 gene-disease validity record.

selected_evidence.snippet: The core phenotype of this HSP syndrome consists of very early-onset (<2 years) spastic paraplegia, intellectual disability, and a specific pattern of brain abnormalities on cerebral imaging.

value.name: SPG70
value.description: SPG70, attributed to MARS1 (methionyl-tRNA synthetase 1). This is the most thinly evidenced row on the entry: a PubMed search for the SPG70 designation and for MARS1/MARS together with spastic paraplegia returned no dedicated SPG70 report, and the human evidence cited here is a childhood-onset HSP case series in which MARS was the confirmed genetic etiology in two of sixteen patients. ClinGen has not curated MARS1 against any HSP entity; its only MARS1 record is Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (Limited, autosomal dominant). The autosomal recessive designation follows the bound MONDO class label.

assertion.name: MARS1
assertion.notes: PubMed searches run 2026-09-26 for the SPG70 designation ("spastic paraplegia 70", SPG70 hereditary spastic paraplegia) and for MARS1 or MARS together with spastic paraplegia returned no dedicated SPG70 report, so the human evidence cited here is a childhood-onset HSP case series in which MARS was the confirmed genetic etiology in two of sixteen patients. The committed ClinGen gene-validity snapshot holds one MARS1 record, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (Limited, autosomal dominant), and none against an HSP entity. The autosomal recessive mode recorded here follows the bound MONDO class label rather than a cited study.

selected_evidence.snippet: Genetically confirmed etiologies included SPAST (3 patients), MARS (2), KIF1A (2), KIF5A (1), SACS (1), SPG7 (1), REEP1 (1), PNPT1 (1), MT-ATP6 (1), and ATL1 (1).

value.name: SPG15
value.description: SPG15, caused by biallelic truncating ZFYVE26 (spastizin) variants; six different truncating mutations segregated with disease in eight families whose phenotype included variable features of Kjellin syndrome. Spastizin colocalizes partially with endoplasmic reticulum and endosomal markers, which is why ZFYVE26 is also bound on the endolysosomal and ESCRT membrane-traffic node. The ZFYVE26 record in `genetic` points at this row. ClinGen has no ZFYVE26 gene-disease validity record.

value.name: SPG39
value.description: SPG39, the spastic-paraplegia presentation of the PNPLA6 disorder spectrum, which also includes Gordon-Holmes, Boucher-Neuhauser, Oliver-McFarlane and Laurence-Moon syndromes. dismech curates the ataxia-hypogonadism-choroidal dystrophy end of that spectrum separately as Boucher-Neuhauser_Syndrome; this row carries the spastic-paraplegia end. ClinGen's Definitive PNPLA6 record for spastic paraplegia is filed against its own entity (PNPLA6-related spastic paraplegia with or without ataxia, MONDO:0100149) rather than against the SPG39 class bound here.

assertion.name: PNPLA6
assertion.notes: ClinGen files its Definitive PNPLA6 spastic-paraplegia record against its own entity, PNPLA6-related spastic paraplegia with or without ataxia (MONDO:0100149), rather than against the SPG39 class bound on this subtype; its second PNPLA6 record is the retinal dystrophy-ataxia-pituitary hormone abnormality-hypogonadism syndrome (MONDO:0100155), whose Boucher-Neuhauser presentation is a separate dismech entry.

selected_evidence.snippet: A wide spectrum of neurodegenerative diseases has been associated with pathogenic variants in the PNPLA6 (patatin-like phospholipase domain-containing protein 6) gene, including spastic paraplegia type 39, Gordon-Holmes, Boucher-Neuhauser, Oliver-Mc Farlane, and Laurence-Moon syndromes.

value.name: SPG43
value.description: SPG43, caused by a homozygous C19orf12 missense variant first reported in two Malian sisters. C19orf12 is allelic with neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation, which dismech curates in Neurodegeneration_With_Brain_Iron_Accumulation; the two presentations are distinguished in the defining report by brain imaging, which showed no iron deposition in the SPG43 subjects. ClinGen's only C19orf12 records are for neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation 4.

assertion.name: C19orf12
assertion.notes: Allelic with neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation, curated in dismech as Neurodegeneration_With_Brain_Iron_Accumulation; the committed ClinGen snapshot holds two C19orf12 records, both against neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation 4 (MONDO:0013674), and none against SPG43.

selected_evidence.snippet: We report here the genetic basis for a form of progressive hereditary spastic paraplegia (SPG43) previously described in two Malian sisters. Exome sequencing revealed a homozygous missense variant (c.187G>C; p.Ala63Pro) in C19orf12

value.name: SPG85
value.description: SPG85, caused by bi-allelic RNF170 variants in four unrelated families. RNF170 is the ubiquitin E3 ligase that targets inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors for degradation, which is why it is bound on the endoplasmic reticulum calcium-release node alongside ERLIN2. The dominant RNF170 disease at the other end of the same allelic series, autosomal dominant sensory ataxia 1, is curated separately as Autosomal_Dominant_Sensory_Ataxia_1, which already records SPG85 as a differential diagnosis. ClinGen has no RNF170 gene-disease validity record.

assertion.name: RNF170
assertion.notes: The dominant disease at the other end of the same RNF170 allelic series, autosomal dominant sensory ataxia 1 (MONDO:0012166), is a separate dismech entry which already records SPG85 as a differential diagnosis rather than as one of its own manifestations.

selected_evidence.snippet: We provide evidence that mutations in the ubiquitin E3 ligase gene RNF170, which targets inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors for degradation, are the likely cause of autosomal recessive HSP in four unrelated families

value.name: SPG57
value.description: SPG57, caused by homozygous TFG variants. Two consanguineous Iranian families carrying homozygous TFG missense variants were reported with early-onset progressive muscle weakness, spasticity and further neurological features. ClinGen has no TFG gene-disease validity record.

selected_evidence.snippet: the tropomyosin-receptor kinase fused gene (TFG) has been linked to diverse hereditary neurodegenerative disorders, including a very rare complex hereditary spastic paraplegia, named spastic paraplegia type 57 (SPG57)

value.name: SCA35
value.description: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 35 was described as an adult-onset progressive ataxia with torticollis caused by TGM6 variants encoding transglutaminase 6. assertion.name: STUB1 variants associated with recessive ataxia
assertion.notes: SCAR16 requires two pathogenic STUB1 alleles, homozygous or compound heterozygous. Reported alleles span the tetratricopeptide-repeat, coiled-coil and U-box domains and include missense, nonsense and frameshift changes; the index allele is the U-box missense p.Thr246Met. value.name: NPPA-related
value.description: Familial AF linked to variants in NPPA, encoding the atrial natriuretic peptide precursor. The mechanism is not a channel defect: a frameshift produces a circulating chimeric peptide, and the proposal is that this peptide, rather than loss of the normal one, shortens the atrial action potential. The circulating peptide is documented in human carriers, but the shortening step is shown in isolated perfused rat heart rather than in human atrium, so the peptide-to-substrate link remains an inference from a model system.

assertion.name: NPPA variants
assertion.features: Variants in NPPA (atrial natriuretic peptide precursor) are linked to familial AF.
assertion.notes: NPPA is the one locus in this entry whose product is a circulating hormone rather than an ion channel or a junctional protein. The defining family was mapped by linkage to 1p36-p35 and carries a heterozygous frameshift; the mutant peptide circulates at high concentration and shortens the atrial action potential, which is how the entry connects it to the shared re-entry-prone substrate.

selected_evidence.snippet: shortened atrial action potentials were seen in an isolated heart model, creating a possible substrate for atrial fibrillation

assertion.name: KCNE2 gain-of-function variants
assertion.features: Gain-of-function variants in the potassium-channel beta subunit KCNE2 are associated with familial AF through enhancement of cardiac potassium current.
assertion.notes: The reported lesion is a single recurrent substitution, R27C, found in 2 of 28 unrelated Chinese AF kindreds, cosegregating with disease in both and absent from 462 controls. Its functional effect parallels KCNQ1 S140G - a gain of function on the KCNQ1-KCNE2 channel - which is why the two are modelled on the same repolarization-shortening arm of this entry.

selected_evidence.snippet: Similar to KCNQ1 S140G, the mutation had a gain-of-function effect on the KCNQ1-KCNE2 channel; unlike long QT syndrome-associated KCNE2 mutations, it did not alter HERG-KCNE2 current.

value.name: SCN1B-related
value.display_name: SCN1B sodium channel beta-1 familial AF
value.description: AF associated with variants in SCN1B, encoding the sodium channel beta-1 subunit, which modulates Nav1.5 gating kinetics and membrane expression. The reported variants reduce SCN5A-mediated current, placing this subtype with the reduced-sodium-current arm rather than the repolarization arm. The index report is a case-control screen of 480 AF patients rather than a pedigree study, so these are susceptibility variants absent from controls rather than demonstrated Mendelian segregation.

assertion.name: SCN1B loss-of-function variants
assertion.association: Reported in AF probands without family segregation
assertion.features: Two nonsynonymous variants, R85H and D153N, identified in AF probands and absent from controls; both reduce SCN5A-mediated current when coexpressed.
assertion.notes:
SCN1B and SCN2B were reported together in one screen of 480 AF patients against 548 controls. The variants are rare, at conserved residues, absent from controls, and reduce sodium current in heterologous expression - but the report describes probands rather than pedigrees, so cosegregation is not established and the grading here is UNKNOWN.
A detail worth carrying: three of the four beta-subunit variant carriers had saddleback right-precordial ST elevation, which places these variants in the Brugada-overlap part of the sodium-channel spectrum rather than in isolated AF.

selected_evidence.snippet: In 3 of 4 mutation carriers, the ECGs showed saddleback-type ST-segment elevation in the right precordial leads.

value.name: KCNA5-related
value.description: Familial AF caused by loss-of-function variants in KCNA5, encoding the voltage-gated potassium channel Kv1.5 (ultra-rapid delayed rectifier current, IKur), which is predominantly expressed in atrial cardiomyocytes. Loss of IKur prolongs atrial action potential duration and may predispose to early afterdepolarizations and AF. This subtype runs the entry's main mechanism backwards: the potassium-channel arm shortens the atrial action potential and this one lengthens it, so a shortened refractory period is not a necessary condition for familial AF.

assertion.name: KCNA5 loss-of-function variants
assertion.features: A heterozygous nonsense variant, E375X, truncates Kv1.5 before the voltage sensor and pore, abolishing the atrial-selective ultrarapid delayed rectifier current IKur and acting dominant-negatively on the wild-type channel.
assertion.notes:
KCNA5 runs opposite to the potassium-channel subtypes above: KCNQ1, KCNE2 and KCNJ2 act by gain of function and shorten the atrial action potential, whereas KCNA5 loss of IKur prolongs it and produces early afterdepolarization and triggered activity. Both routes converge on an arrhythmogenic atrium, which is worth keeping visible because it means action potential shortening is not a necessary feature of monogenic AF.
The channel is described by its discoverers as expressed in human atria, which is the reason a defect in it produces an atrial arrhythmia.

selected_evidence.snippet: Loss of channel function translated into action potential prolongation and early after-depolarization in human atrial myocytes, increasing vulnerability to stress-provoked triggered activity.

value.name: SCN5A-related

assertion.name: SCN5A variants
assertion.features: Cardiac sodium-channel SCN5A variants are associated with familial AF as part of the broader SCN5A arrhythmia spectrum.
assertion.notes: Graded RISK_FACTOR rather than CAUSATIVE deliberately. The largest resequencing study found novel variants in 2.7% of AF probands with cosegregation in six informative families, but its own conclusion is that such variants "may predispose" to AF, and a further 3.2% of probands carried rare variants already attributed to long-QT or Brugada syndrome. SCN5A is therefore better read as a shared arrhythmia-susceptibility locus whose AF phenotype overlaps other sodium-channel syndromes than as a dedicated familial-AF gene.

selected_evidence.snippet: Mutations or rare variants in SCN5A may predispose patients with or without underlying heart disease to AF.

assertion.features: Gain-of-function KCNJ2 (Kir2.1) variants such as V93I increase the inward-rectifier IK1 current and shorten atrial repolarization.

value.name: NUP155-related
value.description: Autosomal recessive familial AF caused by loss-of-function variants in NUP155, encoding nucleoporin 155, a component of the nuclear pore complex important for nucleocytoplasmic transport and cardiac gene expression. Associated with a severe phenotype including sudden cardiac death in young individuals.

assertion.name: NUP155 biallelic loss-of-function variants
assertion.features: A homozygous R391H substitution in the nucleoporin NUP155 that cosegregates with AF in the family in which the 5p13 locus was mapped, mislocalizes the protein, and reduces nuclear envelope permeability.
assertion.notes: The only nuclear pore gene in this entry, and the one whose mechanism is furthest from ion flux: the reported defect is in nucleocytoplasmic transport, specifically of Hsp70 message and protein. It is also the strongest of the newer loci on human-plus-model evidence, since the heterozygous knockout mouse reproduces the AF phenotype even though the human variant is homozygous.

selected_evidence.snippet: The R391H mutation and reduction of NUP155 are associated with inhibition of both export of Hsp70 mRNA and nuclear import of Hsp70 protein.

value.name: MYL4-related
value.display_name: MYL4 (atrial myosin light chain) familial AF
value.description: Autosomal recessive familial AF caused by loss-of-function variants in MYL4, encoding the atrial-specific essential myosin light chain. Associated with early-onset AF, atrial myopathy, and progressive atrial cardiomyopathy. Unlike the channelopathy subtypes, this one is a structural atrial disease, so the entry's framing of familial AF as arising in structurally normal hearts does not hold here.

assertion.name: MYL4 biallelic loss-of-function variant
assertion.features: A rare frameshift deletion, c.234delC, in the atrial-specific essential myosin light chain, fully penetrant for early-onset AF in the homozygous state.
assertion.notes:
MYL4 is the clearest demonstration in this entry that a monogenic AF gene need not be a channel: the product is the atrial-selective essential myosin light chain, and the phenotype is an atrial cardiomyopathy that includes sick sinus syndrome, stroke and sudden death alongside the arrhythmia. An independent family, reported separately, cosegregated a different MYL4 missense variant with atrial standstill, and knock-in and knockout rats reproduced the progressive electrical, contractile and fibrotic phenotype.
It is also the only locus here found by a population approach rather than by following a family, which is why the penetrance statement is unusually strong for this list. No case fraction is recorded: the study reports the allelic frequency and a homozygote count rather than a share of cases, and computing one from those two numbers would not be a reported figure.

selected_evidence.snippet: Three of the homozygotes had received pacemaker implantations due to sick sinus syndrome, three had suffered an ischemic stroke, and one suffered sudden cardiac death.

assertion.name: TRIO
assertion.notes: Illustrates the cytoskeletal/Rho GTPase module: TRIO is a Dbl-family guanine nucleotide exchange factor that activates Rac1 and controls actin dynamics in developing neurons. Included here with two explicit caveats that make it instructive rather than clean. First, the best-characterised TRIO series reports microcephaly and dysmorphism alongside the ID, so this gene-disease pair sits on the syndromic side of an unstable boundary. Second, that series includes an autosomal dominant frameshift that SEGREGATED through a family as well as de novo missense variants, demonstrating that the class is not exclusively de novo. Both caveats argue against treating "autosomal dominant" and "de novo" as synonyms. A third caveat is that the head-size feature is not directionally fixed: TRIO-related disease includes both MRD44 with microcephaly and MRD63 with macrocephaly. The dedicated TRIO-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder entry now models that domain-resolved, RAC1-direction-dependent split and is the canonical home for TRIO variants and mechanisms. TRIO is retained here only as a boundary exemplar, not as a clean non-syndromic gene; the cephalic and dysmorphic findings illustrate why umbrella AD-NSID membership is partial (see GitHub issue 6041).

selected_evidence.snippet: Trio is a Dbl family guanine nucleotide exchange factor (GEF) and a major regulator of neuronal development, controlling actin cytoskeleton dynamics by activating the GTPase Rac1.

value.name: CMS19
value.description: CMS caused by biallelic variants in COL13A1, a single-pass transmembrane collagen enriched at the neuromuscular junction that is essential for the maturation and maintenance of endplate AChRs. All reported patients developed respiratory distress and weak sucking at birth, with facial, bulbar, respiratory and truncal weakness while the limb muscles are relatively spared. Cholinesterase inhibitors are ineffective, whereas salbutamol and amifampridine are effective.

assertion.name: COL13A1
assertion.notes: COL13A1 encodes a single-pass transmembrane collagen enriched at the neuromuscular junction that is required for the maturation and maintenance of endplate acetylcholine receptors. Biallelic variants cause CMS19, a synaptic-compartment CMS in which cholinesterase inhibitors are ineffective but salbutamol and amifampridine help.

selected_evidence.snippet: All patients developed respiratory distress and weak sucking at birth

value.name: CMS9
value.description: CMS caused by defective AChR clustering, from biallelic variants in MUSK. Agrin-bound LRP4 induces MuSK phosphorylation, and phosphorylated MuSK in turn phosphorylates the AChR beta-1 subunit, which binds rapsyn to form endplate AChR clusters. Cholinesterase inhibitors are effective in some patients and worsen weakness in others, while amifampridine and salbutamol are mildly or markedly effective.

assertion.name: MUSK
assertion.notes: MUSK encodes the muscle-specific receptor tyrosine kinase, the central hub of agrin-LRP4-MuSK-DOK7-rapsyn signaling that drives AChR clustering. MUSK-CMS has a variable phenotype and a notably high rate of ICU admission.

value.name: CMS22
value.description: CMS caused by defective recycling of acetylcholine, from loss-of-function variants in PREPL, a serine peptidase whose physiological substrate is unknown. PREPL loss does not cause endplate AChR deficiency; it inhibits refilling of acetylcholine into synaptic vesicles, reduces the number of releasable quanta and lowers the probability of vesicular release. PREPL and SLC3A1 are encoded on opposite strands and overlap at their 3-prime ends, so a deletion spanning both gives hypotonia-cystinuria syndrome. Ten reported patients, including those with the contiguous deletion, were initially diagnosed as Prader-Willi syndrome. Cholinesterase inhibitors are effective.

assertion.name: PREPL
assertion.notes: PREPL encodes a serine peptidase of unknown physiological substrate whose loss impairs refilling of synaptic vesicles with acetylcholine. Biallelic loss-of-function variants cause CMS22; because PREPL overlaps SLC3A1 at its 3-prime end, a deletion spanning both genes gives hypotonia-cystinuria syndrome instead.

selected_evidence.snippet: Ten patients with PREPL-CMS including HCS were initially diagnosed as Prader-Willi syndrome

value.name: Presynaptic
value.description: Defects in acetylcholine (ACh) synthesis, vesicular packaging, or release at the motor nerve terminal. CHAT (choline acetyltransferase) is the commonest presynaptic gene; other genes include SLC5A7, SLC18A3, SNAP25, SYT2, VAMP1, and UNC13A. Presynaptic CMS comprise roughly 5-10% of all CMS and frequently present prenatally/neonatally with a severe phenotype that can include arthrogryposis, developmental delay, and episodic/sudden apneic crises (classically CHAT-CMS, "CMS with episodic apnea").

mondo_mappings.mapping_justification: MONDO:0009689 (congenital myasthenic syndrome 6) is defined in MONDO as CMS caused specifically by CHAT mutations and is_a MONDO:0700466 (presynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome); it is narrower than this Presynaptic subtype, which also covers SLC5A7-, SLC18A3-, SNAP25-, SYT2-, VAMP1-, and UNC13A-related presynaptic CMS. CHAT-CMS is modeled here as the commonest presynaptic gene, with a dedicated CHAT genetic entry below, and is curated in full as Congenital_Myasthenic_Syndrome_6.yaml.

assertion.name: SYT2
assertion.notes: SYT2 encodes synaptotagmin-2, the fast calcium sensor that couples the presynaptic calcium transient to SNARE-mediated vesicle fusion. Hemiallelic and biallelic variants cause CMS7A and CMS7B respectively, which are curated as their own Disease entry (kb/disorders/Congenital_Myasthenic_Syndrome_7.yaml, MONDO:0014468); SYT2 is recorded here so the umbrella entry's gene list is complete.

selected_evidence.snippet: Synaptotagmin 2 (SYT2) senses Ca2+ ions entering into the nerve terminal through P/Q-type calcium channel and triggers the formation of the SNARE complex that releases ACh in synaptic vesicles to the synaptic space

value.name: CMS20
value.description: CMS caused by defective recycling of acetylcholine, from biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC5A7, the high-affinity choline transporter that takes choline up into the nerve terminal. Hemiallelic frameshifting variants of the same gene instead cause autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuropathy type VIIA, and why comparable reductions in transporter activity give two different phenotypes remains unknown. The presentation is neonatal-onset episodic apnea with hypotonia, weakness and weak crying. Cholinesterase inhibitors are effective and ephedrine adds benefit, whereas amifampridine is ineffective.

assertion.name: SLC5A7
assertion.notes: SLC5A7 encodes the high-affinity choline transporter that takes choline back up into the motor nerve terminal for acetylcholine resynthesis. Biallelic loss-of-function variants cause CMS20 with neonatal episodic apnea; hemiallelic frameshifting variants of the same gene instead cause autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuropathy type VIIA.

selected_evidence.snippet: High affinity choline transporter (ChT, SLC5A7) expressed at the nerve terminal membrane uptakes choline to the nerve terminal

value.name: CMS21
value.description: CMS caused by defective recycling of acetylcholine, from biallelic variants in SLC18A3, the vesicular acetylcholine transporter that loads newly synthesized acetylcholine into synaptic vesicles. SLC18A3 lies within the first intron of CHAT, a nested arrangement conserved as far back as C. elegans. Patients show severe weakness at birth with hypotonia, arthrogryposis and respiratory distress, and a decremental CMAP may appear only after isometric contraction. Cholinesterase inhibitors, ephedrine and amifampridine are effective.

assertion.name: SLC18A3
assertion.notes: SLC18A3 encodes the vesicular acetylcholine transporter, which loads newly synthesized acetylcholine into synaptic vesicles, and is encoded within the first intron of CHAT. Biallelic variants cause CMS21, presenting with severe neonatal weakness, arthrogryposis and respiratory distress.

selected_evidence.snippet: Vesicular acetylcholine transporter (vAChT, SLC18A3) transports synthesized ACh to the synaptic vesicle

value.name: CMS23
value.description: CMS caused by defective nerve terminal formation, from biallelic variants in SLC25A1, a mitochondrial inner-membrane transporter whose variants also cause combined D-2- and L-2-hydroxyglutaric aciduria. Limb myasthenia and palpebral ptosis are the shared clinical features. Cholinesterase inhibitors and amifampridine are generally ineffective.

assertion.name: SLC25A1
assertion.notes: SLC25A1 encodes a mitochondrial inner-membrane transporter. selected_evidence.snippet: SLC25A1-CMS is thus predicted to be caused by presynaptic defects

assertion.name: SCN3B variants
assertion.features: SCN3B encodes the auxiliary beta-3 subunit of the cardiac voltage-gated sodium channel and is the gene behind the numbered series term Brugada syndrome 7 (MONDO:0013146). The association rests principally on two variants: L10P, reported in a single American proband, and V110I, found in 3 of 178 SCN5A-negative Japanese patients. Both were reported to impair cytoplasmic trafficking of Nav1.5 and reduce sodium current in transfected cells, converging on the same depolarization-reserve node this entry already curates for SCN5A. A third variant, T138del, was reported in 2025 with preserved beta-3 surface expression and preserved Nav1.5 interaction but reduced peak current, so reduced sodium current rather than mistrafficking is the common thread. The gene-disease claim nonetheless failed reappraisal: no report provided informative segregation data, and both of the originally implicated variants were subsequently found at a heterozygosity frequency of about 1 in 2500 in public population databases, which the ClinGen Brugada gene-validity reappraisal judged to be at or above the population prevalence of Brugada syndrome and therefore incompatible with a highly penetrant monogenic causal role. That reappraisal reclassified SCN3B, with 19 other curated Brugada genes, as disputed. Two further observations point the same way: L10P, the original Brugada allele, was independently reported in a lone atrial fibrillation cohort. The in vivo evidence, by contrast, cuts toward the mechanism rather than against it: the Scn3b-null mouse has reduced peak sodium current in ventricular myocytes and inducible ventricular tachycardia, which its authors describe as resembling Scn5a heterozygous hearts, alongside sinoatrial and atrioventricular conduction disease. What that model cannot settle is the human allele question, since it is a homozygous null while the reported patient variants are heterozygous. SCN3B is therefore curated as part of the disputed non-SCN5A heterogeneity rather than as a validated monogenic cause: the mechanism is plausible and supported in vivo, and the specific reported alleles are what fail. ClinGen has since gone further than the 2018 reappraisal: its Hereditary Cardiovascular Disease Gene Curation Expert Panel classified SCN3B for Brugada syndrome as refuted in December 2025, not merely disputed. This record keeps `relationship_type: DISPUTED` because that enum has no refuted value, and the refutation is stated here and carried by the ClinGen evidence item below.

value.description: Best-supported monogenic Brugada subtype. assertion.name: SCN5A loss-of-function variants
assertion.features: SCN5A is the strongest monogenic Brugada gene and defines the classic NaV1.5 loss-of-function subtype. SCN5A accounts for a minority of all clinically diagnosed Brugada syndrome but dominates the curated high-confidence variant literature and often marks a more severe phenotype. It is the only one of the 21 genes the ClinGen Brugada reappraisal curated that reached a definitive classification, and ClinGen's current assertion is definitive — made not against Brugada syndrome itself but against MONDO:1010181 SCN5A-related cardiac rhythm disorder, the gene-named concept that MONDO also uses as the second parent of Brugada syndrome 1. That routing is why MONDO carries no direct causal-gene edge on MONDO:0011001: the gene is inherited from the gene-named parent, so a gene-keyed comparison over the numbered Brugada series does not see the SCN5A form at all.

assertion.notes: Receptor-regulated SMAD and downstream effector of TGF-beta and NODAL signalling.
